attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own June 2024 essay and re-endorses it in his own post. A self-quote counts as his claim.

semantics.note: 'Never will be' is firm, unhedged language about an outcome with no deadline. The 'on their own' qualifier is kept. The present-tense premise is folded into the proposition, which is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading AGI as broadly human-level general ability is the ordinary informed reading. Requiring an impossibility result for support and an independently validated LLM-only AGI for contradiction is fair to an unbounded 'never'.

evidence.note: ARC Prize's independent evaluation of Astra (Sept 2026, before the cutoff) reports large gains but says outright that it does not claim AGI. It neither establishes LLM-only AGI nor proves impossibility.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended 'never' forecast. The packet contains no independently validated LLM-only AGI demonstration, which would contradict it, and no general impossibility result, which would support it. ARC Prize's Astra evaluation is material progress but explicitly is not an AGI finding. The evidence leaves the outcome unsettled.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words from his June essay, quoted and endorsed in this post.

semantics.note: The context (not AGI, scaling not 'All You Need') supports reading 'enough' as enough for AGI. Treating it as a firm, lasting limit is reasonable, and 'alone' is kept.

contract.note: Defining scaling as more size, data and compute on the same method is an ordinary reading, and the contract flags the RL and inference-compute question. The support and contradiction conditions are balanced.

evidence.note: A peer-reviewed study (Oct 14, 2026) finds that compute explains most frontier performance differences in 2022–25 models. It does not address whether scale is sufficient for AGI.
OpenAI's own disclosure of Astra says it combines pre-training, RL and alignment work. It does not isolate scaling alone and does not show AGI.
The AGI Society (dated Sept 2026; the page says Sept 10) finds the published evidence insufficient to conclude Astra is AGI. It is not a proof that scaling has a limit.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended claim about a lasting limit on scaling. The packet shows neither AGI reached through scaling alone, which would contradict it, nor a conclusive limitation result, which would support it. Astra's development used several methods and has not been independently validated as AGI. The outcome remains unsettled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statement in his own post.

semantics.note: A historical stock-move claim. Both figures and both periods are preserved.

contract.note: The contract chooses closing prices, a July 5 to Aug 5 month, and whole-number rounding. These are ordinary, fair readings. The result depends on them, but the speaker supplied no other measure.

evidence.note: Yahoo split-adjusted closes: 125.83 (Jul 5), 107.27 (Aug 2), 100.45 (Aug 5). That is a 6.36% drop for the day and 20.17% for the month, rounding to 6% and 20%.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's closing-price reading, NVDA fell 6.36% on Aug 5, 2024 and 20.17% from the Jul 5 close. Both round to the figures stated. The packet notes no counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of OpenAI's announcement.

semantics.note: This reports an announcement made that day. The proposition keeps 'see GPT-5' and the next-event scope.

contract.note: Reading the next event as DevDay 2024, and treating GPT-5 as standing for the next flagship model, is the ordinary informed reading of the time.

evidence.note: TechCrunch (Aug 5, 2024) quotes an OpenAI spokesperson saying the company does not plan to announce its next model at DevDay, and reports a scaled-down event format.

reviews.rationale: A same-day TechCrunch report directly quotes OpenAI saying it would not announce its next model at DevDay and describes a quieter format. That matches both the tempered expectations and the no-GPT-5-at-the-event description. 'Next model' rather than 'GPT-5' by name is a minor paraphrase the contract accounts for.
